In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that the use of HMM for optical music recognition of typographic prints is feasible and can be applied to music prints of different origins and quality.
our experiments have shown that the use of Hidden Markov Models is a promising and effective technique for the Optical Music Recognition of typographic music.

the HMMs used in this paper have proved to be a useful technique for the Optical Music Recognition of early typographic prints, and that this technique is robust enough to be able to cope with the poor quality images scanned directly from the original microfilm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a technique to automatically recognize music symbols from typographical music prints.
, for the music prints we have examined, we have achieved a recognition rate of 98% for note symbols, 100% for bar lines and 99% for key signatures.
, using our method, it is possible to obtain good optical music recognition rates even with low resolution and poor quality images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recognition of typographic music is possible using a simple approach, even when the quality of the input images is not very good.
, for typographic music prints, it is possible to obtain good recognition results without the need for complex preprocessing.
the use of simple features, combined with a good model, can lead to a robust recognition process, even when applied to a challenging problem.
